text:
kevin: FYI ran into a bundler + types mismatch when consuming the JS SDK from a pnpm workspace targeting edge. minimal repro included below. anyone seen this exact combo?

kevin: tl;dr: app (pnpm hoisted workspace) imports `import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'` and bundling with vite + esbuild plugin produced a runtime where `Redwood.createClient` is undefined. webpack build on same repo worked.

kevin: short repro notes:
1) monorepo (pnpm) with hoisting enabled (node_modules hoisted to root).
2) frontend workspace has `type: module` and depends on `redwood-sdk` (published with dist/esm + dist/cjs + types).
3) vite build (using default esbuild transform) -> dev build ok, prod build -> edge runtime error: `TypeError: Redwood.createClient is not a function`.

ana: do you have multiple copies of the SDK installed (root + workspace)? pnpm hoisting can cause dedupe or flattened installs where different package.json `exports` are resolved by different tools.

kevin: yes, root has a hoisted copy and workspace has a linked copy, but package-lock shows single version. interestingly the emitted bundle contains `var defaultExport = { createClient: ... }` and also a named `exports.createClient = ...` shim; the runtime shape differs between bundlers.

pri: common root cause: mismatch between runtime JS shape and published typings. If your .d.ts declares `export default` but bundler ends up pulling the CJS entry, consumers without `esModuleInterop` will import differently. Did you check the built `.d.ts` referenced by `types` field?

kevin: types points to `dist/types/index.d.ts` which has `export default interface RedwoodClient {}` and `export function createClient(opts?: any): RedwoodClient`. so default + named both declared.

sam: double-declaring default + named is brittle across bundlers. Also pnpm's hoisting and package managers that rewrite imports (Metro, esbuild) sometimes transform `import` to `require` in edge builds, forcing the `require` branch of `exports`. What does your package.json `exports` look like?

kevin: "exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" }, "./package.json": "./package.json" }

pri: that is the right shape, but note some bundlers ignore `exports` when resolving subpath imports or when inline-optimizing. For vite you can try `optimizeDeps.include: ['redwood-sdk']` to force pre-bundling, or exclude to force runtime ESM resolution depending on where the problem lies.

ana: another gotcha: rollup/webpack respect `mainFields` ordering. webpack by default will check `browser`, `module`, then `main`. If your package has a `browser` field or tool injects one, resolution can change. check `resolve.mainFields` in webpack and `package.json` fields.

kevin: repro repo: private link (internal) with two apps: /vite-app and /webpack-app. vite-app fails in canary deploy; webpack-app works. I'll paste CI stack: `Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading "createClient") at file:///.netlify/functions/edge-handler.js:56:21`.

sam: quick local diagnostics: in the built bundle open the top-level import helper. If you see something like `var __toESM = (mod) => mod && mod.__esModule ? mod : { default: mod }`, then named vs default might be swapped. Also log `Object.keys(Redwood)` in the edge handler to inspect shape.

pri: for typings fix: consider publishing only named exports in types and provide a tiny `index.d.ts` that maps default to the named symbol via `export { createClient as default }` pattern instead of declaring both separately. That reduces ambiguity for TS consumers.

ana: another mitigation for SDK: add an explicit `exports: { ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" }, "./*": { "import": "./dist/esm/*", "require": "./dist/cjs/*" } }` — some bundlers resolve deep imports differently and this helps.

kevin: tried aliasing in vite.config: `resolve.alias['redwood-sdk'] = path.resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules/redwood-sdk/dist/esm/index.js')` and that fixed the runtime shape locally. Not ideal for consumers but useful to confirm root cause.

sam: for webpack, ensure `module.rules` don't transpile node_modules or that the commonjs plugin is configured. For rollup use `@rollup/plugin-commonjs` to normalize cjs/esm interop.

pri: side-note: publish a tiny `interop-test` script in SDK repo that runs `node -e "console.log(require('redwood-sdk'))"` and `node -e "import('redwood-sdk').then(m=>console.log(m))"` on CI to catch mismatches during publish.

kevin: thanks. i'll open SDK issue with the repro, attach the working webpack bundle diffs + failing vite bundle and propose publishing change: switch to named-only exports internally, add an explicit default that references the named function, and extend `exports` with a globby mapping.

build-bot: created ticket SDK-1290 for bundler/hoist interop, assigned to @kevin. CI pipeline 4782 attached.

kevin: will follow up with a PR that updates types and exports plus an examples/interop folder. appreciate the quick pointers. :thumbsup:
